propositions: The bridge has no store-level record of which tracker projects sync and which repos each project's tickets belong to, causing shared snapshots to diff unsynced projects as remote deletions when multiple repos fetch different project subsets.

A new projects_store.py module must implement a projects.json record with version, legacy_default, and projects keys, exposing load_mapping() and resolve_project() functions for CLI, library, and MCP layers.

The resolve_project() tri-state rule returns legacy_default when ticket bridge_project is absent, None when explicitly empty or legacy_default is empty, and the project key when set, ensuring one canonical implementation across inbound/outbound consumers.

The bridge projects subcommand (list, set KEY --repos a,b, remove KEY) must be surfaced through CLI with hardcoded metavar, pinned help.txt listing, library _lib_ops.py, and MCP read/write tools with READ_ONLY annotation enforcement.
An absent projects.json record is legal and reads as empty mapping with None legacy_default (fail-safe until seeded by dependent ensure units); a malformed record raises rather than degrading.
Mapping writes must leave bindings.json and prev_snapshot.json byte-identical, and set on existing keys must replace repos lists idempotently without merge semantics.
